product: commentary — no product (competitor teardown of Resilia oil of oregano)
hook: "Resilia is one of the fastest scaling supplement brands on Meta right now… pushing toward $1M a day in spend, testing something like 6,000 ads."
body: A full strategic teardown of Resilia's parasite angle: cause-RELOCATION — the viewer blames diet/age/stress, the ad relocates blame to parasites behind gut biofilm, then gates the solution (30-50% carvacrol "too weak"; 85% "the only combo strong enough"). The signature roll-call beat: list symptoms (jaw clenching, crawling skin at night, 2-3am wakeups, belly pooch, shoulder pain), each answered "That's parasites." 10+ subpages keep claims off the PDP and dodge bans.
cta: DM "Audit" for a creative audit; link to the top landing page.
idea: The visual-diagnosis roll-call: name the viewer's symptoms one by one and diagnose them all with a single hidden culprit.
sequencing: Scale proof: ~$1M/day, 6,000 ads, one angle.
THE RELOCATION: ordinary blame → parasites behind biofilm.
The roll-call: jaw clenching… "That's parasites." crawling skin… "That's parasites." 2-3am wakeups… "That's parasites."
THE BIOFILM: pre-kill the doctor objection.
The gate: 85% carvacrol, the only combo strong enough.
THE FUNNEL SPLIT: claims on subpages, never the PDP.
WHAT TO STEAL: blame → relocate → gate.
formatting: Long article-style teardown with section headers. Same text as the 94 copy.
why_it_works: The roll-call turns diagnosis into a game the viewer plays along with — each "that's X" lands like a punchline, and by the third one the viewer has self-diagnosed.
what_to_steal: The roll-call rhythm for LC: "Green wrist by noon? That's flash plating. Itchy neck? That's nickel. Faded in a month? That's gold wash." — one culprit per symptom, one mechanism as the only fix. Made for short video and carousel slides.

what_to_steal: The roll-call mechanic for LC's creator program: a monthly "stack roll call" where customers post their LC stacks in comments — same aggregation energy, but the inventory is customer jewelry photos.

hook: "Am I the only one who feels like Gen X creators are still a small part of the UGC community?"
body: A community question post: the poster feels Gen X creators are underrepresented in the UGC community, asks if others agree, and calls "Gen X creators, roll call!" 47 replies. Engagement-bait identity post.
idea: The identity roll-call: name an underrepresented group and summon them — replies become the content.
sequencing: Relatable observation: Gen X creators feel scarce.
Question: agree or am I looking in the wrong places?
Summon: "Gen X creators, roll call!"
Hashtag: #ugc.
formatting: Short text post with emoji. Conversational.
why_it_works: Being summoned by identity is flattering and low-effort to answer, so the replies write themselves — 47 of them here.
what_to_steal: The identity-summon for LC: "Moms who stack, roll call" / "Nurses who never take their jewelry off, roll call" — underrepresented-buyer roll-calls generate comment inventory and cast the next creative wave.
